title: Tenant-scoped geo-gating with tiered fallback model orchestration
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers operating under EU data residency requirements need a deterministic way to guarantee that their inference traffic never leaves EU regions. Existing smart routing routes by latency/cost and falls back to non-EU tiers when capacity is constrained. There is no tenant-scoped allowlist/denylist or tenant-level override to force EU-only routing with deterministic model variant fallback.

This ticket implements a runtime-first policy framework that: 1) allows tenant-level geo policy definitions (EU-only, prefer-EU, allow-global); 2) supports per-tenant allowlists/denylists of regions and routes; 3) enforces strict routing decisions in the serving control plane; and 4) wires fallback model-variant selection so that when an EU-compliant model variant is unavailable, the request is rejected or routed to an explicit on-prem/Dedicated pool rather than silently degrading to non-EU models.

Goals: prevent accidental cross-border data flow for regulated tenants, provide clear failure modes (reject vs. fallback), and expose audit records for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant configuration UI/API accepts a geo_policy field with values: EU_ONLY | PREFER_EU | GLOBAL
Tenant-scoped allowlist/denylist can list region codes (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) and capacity_tiers (dedicated, hosted, private)
Serving control plane evaluates tenant geo policy at routing time and applies precedence: denylist > policy > allowlist > global defaults
If EU_ONLY and no EU-compatible capacity for the requested tier, router rejects and returns 451/upgrade_required with audit log; no request is routed to non-EU endpoints
If PREFER_EU and EU capacity exhausted, router routes to next-best region/tier but annotates the response and emits an alert to the tenant's console and audit stream
Model variant fallback mapping supports explicit tenant-level overrides (e.g., tenant pins to quantized EU variant) and server-side mapping refuses incompatible variants for EU_ONLY tenants
All routing decisions for guarded tenants are logged to audit storage with fields: tenant_id, policy, chosen_region, chosen_tier, model_variant, decision_reason, timestamp
End-to-end integration tests demonstrating EU_ONLY rejection path, PREFER_EU annotated fallback, and allowlist overrides
Performance regression: 95th percentile routing latency increase <= 5ms after policy evaluation added to hot path
implementation_notes: Add tenant.geo_policy and tenant.region_controls to account metadata. Schema will be validated by identity service (IAM).
Extend Policy Decision Point (PDP) to evaluate tenant-scoped policies before global routing heuristics. PDP API change: evaluate(tenant_id, request_meta) -> RoutingDecision with fields as strings.
Router change: call PDP synchronously in pre-routing step; PDP should be cacheable per tenant for 60s but invalidated on tenant config change.
Introduce explicit FailureMode enum: REJECT, FALLBACK_ANNOTATE, FALLBACK_SILENT (avoid for EU_ONLY). Default for EU_ONLY => REJECT, PREFER_EU => FALLBACK_ANNOTATE.
Model catalog: tag model variants with region_compatibility and residency_flags. On model selection, cross-check winner model variant region tag matches tenant policy.
Dedicated/private pools: add metadata so PDP can choose 'on-prem' fallback for EU_ONLY tenants if customer has a private deployment registered in EU.
Audit: pipe decision events to kafka topic 'routing-audit' and to tenant-specific audit storage (s3 prefix) with encryption and retention per compliance settings.
Console: expose policy editor, decision logs filter, and a simulator endpoint where tenant admins can run test requests and see deterministic decision traces.
Edge cases: expired region allowlist entries, multi-tenant shared Dedicated pools, GPU capacity fragmentation. Documented trade-offs below.
design_decisions: Precedence: explicit denylist takes highest priority so tenant can blackhole specific regions even if policy prefers them
Synchronous PDP call kept in path to guarantee correctness; mitigated by short-lived caching to bound added latency
For EU_ONLY, prefer explicit REJECT to avoid silent non-compliance; operators can enable tenant-specific 'on-prem fallback' if customer provides a private endpoint
PREFER_EU should provide visibility (annotation + alert) rather than strict enforcement to preserve availability for non-critical workloads
Do not allow global model autoscaling to override tenant denylist; autoscaler will surface capacity pressure to PDP via capacity metadata instead.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement PDP extension and routing checks behind runtime flag + enable for internal test tenants. Duration: 2 weeks
Phase 2 (limited beta): enable for 5 pilot customers with EU residency needs. Validate audit logs, penalty behavior, and console UX. Duration: 3 weeks
Phase 3 (limited public): enable API/UI for customers to opt-in for EU_ONLY and PREFER_EU. Monitor errors and support tickets. Duration: 2 weeks
Phase 4 (default enforcement): flip runtime flag for all tenants that have explicit geo_policy set. Monitor metrics and rollback plan in place. Duration: 1 week
Rollback: set PDP to 'allow permissive' mode and/or revert flag; metric-based automated rollback if rejection rate > 0.5% for tenants not in pilot
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for PDP policy evaluation logic (denylist/allowlist precedence, policy enum behavior)
Integration test: synthetic tenant with EU_ONLY, no EU capacity -> expect 451 and audit entry
Integration test: PREFER_EU with EU exhausted -> expect successful routing to non-EU with response header 'X-Redwood-Geo-Fallback: true' and audit note
Load test: simulate 10k requests/sec across 100 tenants with mixed policies; verify routing latency (95p) within SLA
Security test: ensure audit logs are only accessible to tenant admins and authorized Redwood SREs; validate encryption at rest
Chaos: kill EU region control plane during beta to observe deterministic REJECT behaviors and customer impact
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboards: 'geo_policy_decisions' (counts by tenant, policy, outcome), 'geo_rejections' (by tenant, reason)
SLOs: track false-positive rejections (customer-reported vs. audit) and latency SLO for policy evaluation
Alerts: paging on sharp increase in EU_ONLY rejection rates or unexpected spikes in fallback routing for PREFER_EU tenants
Telemetry: attach model_variant and chosen_region tags to token billing traces for cost reconciliation
Audit retention: default 90 days in hot storage, configurable per-enterprise contract
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased routing latency on hot path -> Mitigation: cache PDP results, optimize policy evaluation code, perf budget 5ms
Risk: tenants misconfigure policies leading to unintended rejection -> Mitigation: add simulator in console + validation hints and a graceful default (PREFER_EU) when uncertain
Risk: capacity pressure causing large numbers of rejections for EU_ONLY -> Mitigation: surface capacity pressure to customers via console and recommend Dedicated/Private options
Risk: audit log volume and storage costs -> Mitigation: sample low-risk tenants, tier retention by plan, compress events
